column1: ## Part 7 of docs/benchmark-2026-10-27-llm-templates-round4.md: first contact WITH THE CLEAN-UP (values keep to their cells,
## lines set aside filed as NAME.notes, skipped lines no longer lost against a catch-all). The same 98 templates `learn` wrote
## (llm-templates-learn/), plus a new first contact for the 7 the old catch-all guard declined (llm-templates-learn-cleanup/),
## offline (llm_round.sh --round4 --templates round4/llm-templates-learn:<those 7>), 2026-10-27. The 66 inputs whose filed output
## changed were rated again, blind, on CRITERIA.md (rerated=yes); the other 41 are byte-identical and keep part 4's rating.

column7: note

Every input line is accounted for: the Suggested/NEW package lists (4 rows with their section), the 0/3/0/1 summary under named columns, all six Inst/Conf actions split cleanly into package, version, archives and arch, and the three progress lines kept as notes.

Summary line (7 shift/reduce, -Wconflicts-sr), all 7 conflicts with token and example, and all 28 shift/reduce derivation steps with conflict, level, rule and production are kept in stable columns; only alignment whitespace is collapsed (which symbol a level-1 step expands is recoverable from the example).

Every section survives as its own well-named table: 4 conflict lines, all 14 grammar rules (continuation | lines given their lhs), 13 terminals, 5 nonterminals with on-left/on-right, 8 state items with lookaheads and 16 state actions, with headings kept as notes; the only thing not carried is the redundant (lhs) name after each reduce-rule number, which the grammar table already supplies.

All values are kept and the pass/skip/todo/fail/expect counts, the 7-tests/1-file/1.67s run line and the two (fail) results are cleanly named, but each failure diagnostic is scattered: its error message, Expected/Received pair (itself split over two rows) and at-location sit in three separate tables with no test name or key tying them to the failing test, so the record is only reassembled by row order.

All 18 settings land as Section/Group/Key/Value rows with indented keys correctly attached to their parent (Bundler, Ruby, RubyGems, Tools), the build-metadata pair is kept, and both Gemfile/Gemfile.lock contents are filed under their section path, with only markdown headings and fences left as notes.

All 59 AST nodes land one per row with the tree glyphs turned into correct Depth and Parent-address columns (spot-checked through the ForStmt, IfStmt and nested BinaryOperator branches, including both <<<NULL>>> children), node kind, address, source range, location and remaining details in stable columns, and the Dumping total: heading kept as a note and as the Function value.

All seven report sections survive: 106 timer rows (4+4+3+10+81+2+2, Total rows included) carry section, name and each time/percent pair under its own header-named column, with the extra System Time column correctly placed for the two four-column sections, and the six Total Execution Time lines are kept with wall-clock values in a totals table.

Every section survives in a named table keyed by record: all 20 AST-layout fields with offset (bitfield ranges intact), nesting depth, type and name, the three sizeof/align lines, three RecordDecls, all 13 FieldDecls, the three LLVMType/IsZeroInitializable layouts and both CGBitFieldInfo rows with every attribute; the only reduction is that each bitfield's ConstantExpr/IntegerLiteral sub-nodes are collapsed into their BitWidth value (wrapper addresses not kept) and the trailing word definition is dropped, neither substantive.
All 36 trace lines are split into file, line, command and args (the help text glued onto line 1 is kept in a trailing column), and all 10 '--' status messages are in their own dataset.

Version and release timestamp are a named row, all 11 options split into short/long/description (including the long-only and -v|vv|vvv forms), and all 34 commands carry their bracketed aliases in their own column, with the usage line kept as a note and only the ASCII-art banner dropped as decoration.
All 3 legend lines land in a color/meaning table and all 106 warning flags in one row each with correct depth and parent derived from the indentation tree; nothing lost.

All 26 TERM/COLORTERM patterns, 18 file-type colour codes with comments and the 5 extensions are cleanly named and every comment line is kept as a note, but the LINK entry's two-line comment is split: its row ends mid-sentence at instead of a and the continuation (numerical value, the color is as for the file pointed to.) sits only in notes rather than in the LINK comment.

Both sections survive: all eight device/extent summary fields are one named row (units and the 76.5% kept with their values) and all five histogram buckets have range start/end, free extents, free blocks and percent under the header's own names, with the histogram title kept as a note.

All 43 pattern elements land as named columns with correct values and all 50 charset pages keep their page plus 8 words, but the per-value type/binding annotations ((s)/(w) strong/weak binding, (i)/(f) type) are stripped from every element and survive nowhere except the lone charset (s) in notes.

Source header, all 3 function summaries (called/returned/blocks), all 26 annotated source lines (count, line number, source text with indentation) and all 11 branch records (tied to their function and line, taken count, fallthrough/never-executed note) are kept in four well-named tables; nothing lost.

All 5 function and 2 file records land one per row with lines/branches/taken/calls percent and totals plus the .gcov output name, and the overall 73.33% of 30 total is kept, but util.c's 'No calls' line is not recorded (its calls columns are just blank, indistinguishable from the functions where calls were never reported, rather than 0).

All 8 header key-values form a one-row file table with real names and all 48 namespace::attribute lines are split into namespace/attribute/value with nothing lost; only the bare 'attributes:' heading goes to notes.

WORK, modinfo, all 62 packagefile entries and the 11 shell commands (env, command, args, '# internal' note) are kept correctly, but the two importcfg heredocs are merged into one packagefiles table with no column saying which file (importcfg: 5 entries vs importcfg.link: 57) each belongs to, and the two 'cat > ... << EOF' commands are left as skipped notes instead of command rows.

Package name, import path and synopsis form one row, and each of the 9 declarations (type Ring plus 8 funcs) is one row with section, kind, receiver, name, full signature and its complete multi-paragraph doc kept together.

Read as YAML into one 110-column row: each linter's description survives under its name, but the 'Enabled by your configuration' and 'Disabled by your configuration' section headers are dropped so the 5 enabled linters are indistinguishable from the 105 disabled ones, each linter is a column rather than a row with name/description/tags, and the 'wsl [deprecated]' entry is lost entirely.

All 9 issues are one row each with file, line, column, message, linter and source line (caret markers rightly dropped as the column is kept), and the '9 issues' total and the 5 per-linter counts are kept as their own tables.

The flat profile (4 rows, named columns) and the 5 primary call-graph entries are correct, but the 8 caller/callee lines go to a separate table with no link to the entry they belong to and no caller/callee role, so who calls whom is lost (e.g. 'scan 1499999/1499999' cannot be read as scan calling collatz), <spontaneous> is only a note, and the function-index section comes out as 2 rows with empty index and name.

The entry line gives name vt220, alias vt200 and description, and all 107 capabilities land one per row with the right boolean/numeric/string type and exact value (escapes, padding and embedded spaces intact); the source-file comment is kept in notes.

All 90 log lines are accounted for: 16 gc,init settings as one named row, 5 pauses with heap before/after/capacity/duration, 25 phase timings, 20 region transitions (empty target where the input has none), 5 cpu rows and 19 other events with uptime/level/tags/GC id, all under correct columns; only the per-line uptime and tag of the init settings are not kept.

Class, all 8 members with descriptors, all 71 bytecode instructions (member, offset, opcode, operands, constant-pool comment), the 2-row exception table and all 13 LineNumberTable entries are kept with the right member on each row and nothing lost.

Every section survives with real column names: total usage (loaders/classes/shared), the 3-row usage table with every size and percentage, virtual space, all 45 chunk-freelist rows tagged Non-Class/Class/Both plus their 3 totals, the waste table, the chunk header pool, the 13 internal statistics and the 10 settings; the pid and the waste heading's 4.06 MB basis are kept in notes.

All 13 events are filed: 6 GCHeapMemoryPoolUsage and 7 ThreadStart rows with every field (thread names and javaThreadIds split out, N/A parent kept), plus 6 stack frames tied to their event id with method and line; only the '...' truncation marker on the first stack trace is not kept.
The recording header (Version 2.1, Chunks 1, Start, Duration 20 s) is one row and all 52 event types land with Event_Type/Count/Size_(bytes) under the input's own header names.

pid, JVM version and GC, all 12 heap-configuration settings, and the 4 heap-usage spaces with regions, capacity, used, free and used% are correct (the dropped MB figures just repeat the byte counts), but the 'G1 Young Generation:' heading is dropped entirely, so nothing records that Eden and Survivor make up the young generation alongside G1 Old Generation.

All 21 plugin options land one per row with Option/Argument/Description columns and their wrapped multi-line descriptions joined, and the title and trailing pattern-list footer are kept verbatim in notes.

All 26 threads (17 Java plus 9 VM threads, including the truncated unnamed one) have every header field in named columns, all 68 frame/lock/info lines sit in stack_frames keyed by thread and tid, and the timestamp/JVM line and JNI refs counts are filed; the SMR thread-list block is kept verbatim in notes.
Both sections survive as separate datasets, with 19 CPUs and 52 features each one row of name/description, and the section titles and closing usage lines kept in notes.

All command outputs (executable, breakpoint, process events, stop thread, 6 frames, variables, source listing, 4 images) are filed in well-named columns, but the two printed structs from p *it and p *it->next are flattened into one struct_members table of 8 member/value rows with no column saying which expression or type each member belongs to; the (const item)/(item) headers survive only in notes.

The file format, compile-unit header (all fields), all 31 DIEs with offset/depth/tag, and all 124 attributes keyed by DIE offset and tag with parsed values are kept, and only the NULL child terminators go to notes, which the depth column already implies.

Every section survives: the summary key/values, both legends, the 5-row instruction-info table with the MayStore * under the right column, and the per-iteration and by-instruction resource-pressure tables with resource names applied as column headers.

File info, the full ElfHeader (Ident fields flattened into one row, all 21 fields correct) and all 7 sections present in the (truncated) input are one row each with every field under its name; per-flag hex values (SHF_ALLOC (0x2)) are reduced to names but remain derivable from the kept Flags total.

The 4 build steps (step/total/description), all 7 metric rows with their real headers (including both node stat rows), and the hash-load summary line parsed into load/entries/buckets are filed, and the Entering-directory line is kept in notes.

All 15 GC trace lines are one row each with pid, isolate, time, type, before/after heap and committed sizes, pooled, pause and external times, mu values and reason in named columns, and the interleaved program output kept 2667 is kept in notes.

All 47 ops are filed with seq, class, op, flags and next correctly separated, but the indentation that encodes the op-tree nesting is dropped (there is no depth or parent column), so the tree structure cannot be recovered.

All 18 measurements across the five test sections are one row each with a section column, method, ops/sec and usecs/op (n/a kept for fsync_writethrough), and the preamble and section explanations are kept in notes.

All 15 histogram buckets land with correct us/percent/count values, the per-loop time is a kv summary row and the two prose lines (including the 2-second duration) are kept whole in notes; only the '<' of the '< us' header is dropped from the column name.

Class row, all five section counts, all seven methods (section, origin, modifiers, return type and return kind) and all five parameters keyed by method are filed correctly; the per-method parameter-count lines are kept in notes and are derivable anyway.
All five errors land one per row with severity, message, line and file in stable columns, and the 'Tally.pod has 5 pod syntax errors' summary is kept as its own row.

All 80 headerless tab-separated rows are filed byte-identical with sensible pg_settings-style column names (name, context, category, vartype, boot_val, min_val, max_val, short_desc, extra_desc), empty fields preserved.
Every one of the 31 prtstat fields, including the minor/major, user/system/guest/blkio sub-values, lands as a correctly named column in one record, and the section headings are kept in notes.

Module name, summary, reference URL and file are one record, all six functions with signatures, the __all__ data entry and the MODULE REFERENCE and DESCRIPTION prose as one row per section are all filed; nothing substantive is lost.
All 18 formatters are one row each with their aliases, full description and filename globs split into their own column, and the version/copyright line is kept in notes.

Every section survives: session header fields, the progress line, the failure and two pass reports with their source/error/stdout/log kept together per test, all seven short-summary lines with outcome/reason, and the 1/4/1/1 0.03s totals.
All 84 lines of the AST dump become one row each with depth, ancestor path, field name, node type and literal value, every node and leaf (constants, names, empty lists) preserved in order.

All five frames land with file/line/function/code and the traceback they belong to, and all three exceptions with type, message and the chaining sentence that links them; only caret markers and repeated Traceback banners are set aside.

All 55 opcodes land one per row with offset, code, opcode and argument in stable columns (non-ASCII string intact) and the 'highest protocol' summary line is kept as a field/value row; only the nesting indentation is dropped, which is fully implied by the MARK opcodes and their '(MARK at N)' arguments.
All 14 classes (name, bases, line) and all 69 methods (owning class, name, line) are filed in two well-named tables with every value under the right column and nothing dropped.

All five warnings land one per row with file, line, category, message and the source line kept together in named columns, and the ResourceWarning tracemalloc hint is kept intact (category + message) in a separate notes dataset; nothing is lost.
All 6 entries are filed under the real File_Name/Modified/Size headers with the date-time kept whole and the space-containing and non-ASCII filenames intact.

All 13 progress lines, the six biggest-key rows, the sampled-key count, total/avg key length and the six per-type totals (count, size, unit, percent, avg) are filed in correctly named columns; only the comment banner goes to notes.
All seven sample rows land under keys/mem/clients/blocked/requests/connections (plus the empty child column) with values aligned; only the data/load/child group-rule line is set aside as decoration.

All 35 instructions (pos, insn, operands, line, events), both local tables and five locals are filed, but the six '== disasm' ISeq headers went unread into notes so the iseq column is empty on every row, losing which method/block each instruction and local belongs to (and opt_ltlt's [CcCr] events are merged into its operands).

Every section is kept: speed/rows/columns/line as a named settings row, all 17 control characters as named columns, and all 53 flags one per row with the leading '-' correctly turned into enabled yes/no.
All 45 syscalls across the 8 groups land one per row with their @group and the group's description comment attached in stable named columns; nothing is lost.
All 6 [EXTENDED] entries are filed with type, overridden path and drop-in target in named columns, and the '6 overridden configuration files found' summary is kept as a numeric field/value row.

All 56 option lines land as one row each with option and value columns, quoted values (including the long status-format strings and escaped quotes) kept verbatim, and option+value reproduces the input exactly.

All content kept across five linked tables: summary (pid, version 3.22.0, command, 2 errors/2 contexts, 1/1 suppressed), both thread announcements, both races with access/size/address/thread/locks plus the conflicting access and the counter symbol, all 30 stack frames keyed to their context, and banner, program output 2000 and the hint lines kept as notes.

All 24 timing lines are kept with clock, self+sourced, self and description correctly aligned, but the second header row (clock elapsed: other lines) is not applied: the elapsed values of the 15 other lines are filed under the self column, and no elapsed name appears anywhere in the output.

Document properties (version, encoding, URL, standalone), all 31 tree nodes (one row each with type, name, compact flag, depth, an XPath-style path and the exact content including whitespace-only text, the escaped UTF-8 name and the CDATA) and the x namespace declaration on /order are all kept in three well-named datasets.

All 105 field lines are kept in order with correct offset, field name, hex value and decoded text (including the [Bits 1-2] sub-flag, payload previews and the UTF-8 filename), but the added Record/Parent grouping is broken: after each LOCAL HEADER's first six fields the Record key switches to 'CRC', then 'UID', then 'GID' (74 of 105 rows, including every Filename), and UID/GID lose their Extra ID #0002 parent while GID Size is parented to 'UID', so each local header is split into four mislabelled pseudo-records.

All 11 error-log entries land one per row under the input's own headers (IDENTIFIER, TIMESTAMP, T, C, RESOURCE_NAME, DESCRIPTION) with multi-word descriptions kept whole and every value matching the input.

All 28 headerless attribute lines land one per row under apt names (attribute, value, description, user_settable) matching lsattr's own -H header, with the empty location value correctly left blank, multi-word descriptions kept whole and True/True+/False flags intact.

All 38 key/value status lines become one wide record with each key as a column (END APC as END_APC) and every value intact including units, timestamps with offsets, multi-word strings and the 'FW:T2' colon inside FIRMWARE; only trailing padding is trimmed.
All 12 MAC entries are filed with Vlan/Mac_Address/Type/Ports under their real headers, the Total Mac Addresses 12 summary line is kept as a field, and the prompt and title lines are kept as notes.

The CPU utilization line is split into 5s total/interrupt, 1-minute and 5-minute values, and all 14 processes are filed under their real headers with multi-word process names such as IP Input kept intact.

Every section is kept: pool status kv (9 fields), the 7 pool traffic stats, the status of all 3 members, and all 18 member traffic stats with both the ServerSide and General columns, each keyed by pool/member; only the prompt and section labels went to notes.

All 10 fields are filed with domain, type, charset, nullability, default, and the continuation-line collation and CHECK kept on their own field rows; the 4 constraints are filed with type, columns and definition, and both triggers with sequence, type and status.

Runner version/revision/host/token/system ID, all 5 sections with start/end timestamps, duration and title, all 21 output/command lines tagged by section with line numbers (pytest failure and its 1 failed/15 passed/1 skipped summary kept verbatim), and the final ERROR exit code 1 are all present; ANSI/section markers are decoration.

The whole hierarchy is kept in linked tables: the controller (model, slot, Embedded, serial), 2 drive cages, 2 ports, arrays A and B, 3 logical drives (size, RAID, status including Interim Recovery Mode), all 8 physical drives with their array or Unassigned plus the spare flag, and the SEP enclosure (vendor, model, 380, WWID).

All 6 disks are filed under their real headers, with each record's continuation line merged into Block_Device and Raw_Device columns on the same row (two-line records kept together) and every value in its right column.

Schedd name/address/timestamp, all 5 batches under the real OWNER..JOB_IDS header (ID:/DAG: batch names and _ placeholders intact), and both Total lines decomposed into jobs/completed/removed/idle/running/held/suspended are all present.

All 13 interfaces are filed with correct PHY/Protocol/InUti/OutUti/error values, and the flag legend is kept as notes, but the indentation that marks GigabitEthernet0/0/1 and 0/0/2 as members of Eth-Trunk1 is lost: they appear as ordinary top-level rows with no trunk or parent column.

The system name, date/time and all 13 status fields from both kv columns are filed correctly, and the 4 pools are filed under properly combined two-row headers (DB_Fault, Non-DB_Pages, Act-Wait and so on), with the +++++ value kept; the function-key and prompt lines went to notes.

All 5 dbspaces and 6 chunks are filed under the real headers, with the counts, setting, banner and NOTE kept; but the sbspace chunk's Metadata line (13277/9850/13277) goes to a separate chunk_metadata dataset with no chunk number, so it is no longer tied to chunk 5, and the two 'N active, M maximum' rows in counts no longer say which one is dbspaces and which is chunks.

All five sections survive with their real headers: model (1 row), apps (4, telegraf's empty Version kept blank), units (4, leader asterisks kept), machines (4) and offer (1), every value under the right column and blank Message cells preserved.

All 22 interface lines and 7 continuation lines become 29 rows under the real headers (Interface/Admin/Link/Proto/Local/Remote), with the interface, admin, link and proto values filled down onto each extra address or protocol; only the prompt and decoration go to notes.
All 14 klog events are one row each, with severity, date, time, pid, file, line, message and attributes in stable columns, and the multi-line fatal err=<...> block stays in one record.

All three sections are kept under their real headers (5 instance groups, 6 nodes, 3 validation errors), the cluster name and error line become a key-value row, and the section titles and 'Validation Failed' are kept in notes.

All 18 taxa land as rows with percent, clade reads, taxon reads, rank code, taxid and name under correct kraken2 column names; the name indentation is stripped but the rank codes keep the hierarchy recoverable, and the two extra Minimizers columns are merely empty.
All 41 key-value pairs, including the APFS block, land in one record with their real key names and full values; the only other line, 'This disk is an APFS Volume', is kept in notes.

All 18 registry nodes land as rows with name, @location, class, id, state flags, busy count/time and retain split cleanly (including the !registered node and the non-ASCII name), but the tree depth/parent relationships drawn by the +-o/| indentation are lost, so you can no longer tell which interface or device hangs off which hub or controller.

All 36 scalar attributes are filed as one record keyed by attribute name and all 12 items of the 5 list-valued attributes (Authors, ContentTypeTree, EncodingApplications, UsedDates, WhereFroms) as attribute/value rows, with UTF-8 values and (null) preserved; the only nit is that _kMDItemDisplayNameWithExtensions lost its leading underscore in the column name.

All four sections are filed as their own datasets (6 device types, 4 runtimes, 8 devices with the runtime group filled down, and 1 device pair with its watch and phone lines merged), with names, ids, states and unavailable notes all in the right columns.

All 7 interfaces are one row each, with their continuation lines merged; the index, flags, ;;; comments and every key=value (including timestamps that contain spaces) sit under their own key names, and the prompt and flag legend are kept in notes.

All 8 sessions land as rows under the real sp_who2 headers with values correctly aligned (HostName/BlkBy '.', BlkBy 54 on SPID 57, multi-word Command and ProgramName kept whole, empty ProgramName for system SPIDs); only the dash rule and the redundant duplicate SPID column (identical values) are dropped.
All 7 two-line sessions are merged into one row each, and the src/dst IP, port, zone, proto, translated IP/port and vsys are split into correctly named columns; the empty Flag values stay empty.
The 3 metric rows sit under all 34 real column names with the empty SAMPLE/LIBRARY/READ_GROUP columns kept, and the ## header lines (the command line and start time) are kept verbatim in notes.

All 21 lines are kept with correct fields (started/processing/completed requests parsed into method, path, IP, controller, action, status, timings; other lines with severity, timestamp, PID, request ID), but the FATAL event is split: its row in log_entries has an empty Message while the NoMethodError text and its two backtrace frames sit as four separate rows in a separate continuation_lines dataset, linked only by request ID.
All 6 hosts (global plus five nodes) are filed under the input's own 11 column names with every value in place, including the '-' placeholders for global and node04; only the rule line is dropped.

Every section survives under its real headers (the database row, 2 device fragments, the log-only free kbytes value, and 4 device/segment rows), with multi-word values such as dates and status intact, and the '(1 row affected)' and return status lines kept in notes.

All 29 log lines are kept as one row each across four consistent datasets (build-level lines, 3 step headers with step number, total, name and the 1s duration, 15 block lines with time, W/E status, block and message, and 8 ##teamcity service messages split into type, name, duration, message, details and flowId), with every value under the right column.

Held in 'unsorted' with no dataset filed, so none of the six pipe-separated client records (clid, cid, client_database_id, client_nickname, client_type) nor the 'error id=0 msg=ok' status line was extracted.

All four sections survive: session kv (BTEQ version, start time, PID, DB release/version, BTET, UTF8, RC 0), the query with its 6-rows/4-columns/2-seconds summary, all 6 result rows with values under the real column headers (umlauts decoded, NULL '?' kept), and the logon/logoff/1-second elapsed lines kept in notes.

All three entries are filed one row each with the input's own keys as columns (Boot Manager in one dataset, both Boot Loaders together in another), every value under the right key, and the two-line displayorder kept together as one value.

Every section is kept with real names and a Computer/User scope column: the RSOP header and OS kv fields, both settings blocks (DN, last applied, DC, slow-link threshold, domain), 6 applied GPOs, 3 filtered GPOs with their Filtering and WMI Filter values, and all 22 security groups (10 computer + 12 user); only banners and section titles go to notes.

All 5 sessions land as one row each under the real header names, with blank SESSIONNAME kept as empty cells, the '>' current-session marker split into its own column, and the multi-word IDLE TIME and LOGON TIME values intact.

All sections survive and are correctly shaped: the job header (started/source/dest/files/options), 4 directory lines with counts, 8 file lines each tied to its directory with status and size, the 3-line ERROR 32 event kept together as one row, the Dirs/Files/Bytes/Times summary with the sparse Times row aligned correctly under Total/Copied/FAILED/Extras, and the speed and end-time lines.

All 3 task records come out as one row each with all 29 keys as named columns plus the Folder context, and every value, including the quoted Task To Run command and the comma-bearing Power Management and Idle Time values, sits under its own key.

All 18 processes land with the 10 real header names, and every multi-word value (Image Name 'System Idle Process', User Name, Status 'Not Responding', the window titles with spaces, pipes and Unicode) sits whole under the right column.

23 of the 24 privileges are filed correctly under Privilege_Name/Description/State, but the last one (SeDelegateSessionUserImpersonatePrivilege, Disabled) is missing from the table and survives only as an unread raw line in notes.

All 7 connections are filed with the 21 #fields names as headers and every value (including -, (empty) and the ssl,http set) in the right column, the separator/set_separator/empty_field/unset_field/path/open/close metadata is kept as one row, and the #fields/#types header lines are kept in notes.

All 73 key/value attributes of the three entries (including the 8 ATTRIBUTES flags and the wrapped SYSTEM-TIMESTAMP), the 14-row entries-processed count and both IDC messages are kept, but the entry-level PROTECTION-PSWD (NULL) and RACF (NO) line of the CLUSTER is mis-sectioned as SMSDATA rather than left at entry level like IN-CAT, and the protected-entries-suppressed count survives only as a raw note.
